discovery: Cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmological structure
motivation: Guth proposed that a period of exponential expansion in the early universe solves the horizon, flatness and monopole problems. Linde made inflation a working theory through new and chaotic inflation, showing it arises generically from a slowly rolling scalar field. Mukhanov (with the late Chibisov) showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations, stretched to cosmic scales during inflation, seed all structure in the universe, and predicted a nearly scale-invariant spectrum with a slight red tilt. Decades of CMB and large-scale-structure data, culminating in Planck, have confirmed these predictions with striking precision: spatial flatness, adiabatic and nearly Gaussian super-horizon fluctuations, and a spectral index n_s ≈ 0.965, measurably below one. The idea that galaxies are amplified quantum fluctuations is one of the deepest and most surprising in modern physics. It connects quantum field theory to the largest observable scales and now drives the study of cosmological correlators and the search for primordial gravitational waves.
